haiku-low.q1: When the connection returns, when the app comes to the foreground, and every 60 seconds while online.
haiku-low.q2: Push first, uploading queued changes, then pull, downloading the server's change log.
haiku-low.q3: The server detects it by comparing the change's starting version with the note's current version. Not equal means conflict.
haiku-low.q4: The first write to reach the server is stored as the note's version. The losing body is saved as a separate conflict note titled "<original title> (conflict)".
haiku-low.q5: One change, keeping the first change's ID and original starting version, with the latest title and full body.
haiku-low.q6: The server stores each change ID with its result. A repeated ID returns the stored result and applies nothing.
haiku-low.q7: On the phone, as the cursor (highest log sequence number applied). It is saved only together with applying a pulled page, in one local transaction.
haiku-low.q8: The cursor did not move, so the next sync repeats the same pull request. The UI is unchanged until a pull succeeds.
haiku-low.q9: The conflict result gives the conflict note ID and the change leaves the outbox. A later pull brings the newer server version, replacing local title, body and version.
haiku-low.q10: When its push result comes back, either accepted or conflict. A change with no response stays in the outbox.
haiku-low.q11: The local title, body and version are replaced. The queued change stays in the outbox with its old starting version, so it will conflict and its body is saved as a conflict note.
haiku-low.q12: It becomes a new queued change with its own new change ID. Its starting version is the new version if the sent change was accepted; if it conflicts, it keeps the old version and will conflict too.

sonnet.q1: The connection returning, the app coming to the foreground, and a 60-second timer while online (tick skipped if a sync is still running).
sonnet.q2: Push first, then pull. Push repeats in batches until the outbox is empty, then it pulls.
sonnet.q3: The server. It compares the change's starting version with the note's current version. If they are not equal, it is a conflict.
sonnet.q4: The first push to reach the server wins and is accepted (note goes to the next version, logged). The second phone's change has a stale starting version, so the server saves its body as a separate conflict note titled "<title> (conflict)" (new note ID, version 1) and logs it. It also stores the results under the change IDs. Nothing is merged and no text is lost.
sonnet.q5: One collapsed change. It has the original change ID, the original starting version, and the latest title and full body.
sonnet.q6: Each change has a change ID. The server stores every handled change ID with its result. If it sees the ID again, in any batch or later, it returns the stored result and applies nothing.
sonnet.q7: The phone stores a cursor, which is the highest log sequence number it has applied. It is updated only after a page is applied, saved in the same local transaction as applying that page.
sonnet.q8: The cursor did not move past the unapplied page, so the next sync repeats the same pull request. The UI is unchanged until a pull succeeds.
sonnet.q9: The push result says conflict with the conflict note ID. B keeps seeing its own text until it pulls. On the pull it gets the log entries (A's newer version and the conflict note). The version is newer than its local version, so the local title, body and version are replaced and the conflict note is created.
sonnet.q10: When the push result for it comes back, whether accepted or conflict. If there is no response, or the server stops on an error before it, it stays in the outbox.
sonnet.q11: The local title, body and version are replaced by the newer entry. The queued change stays in the outbox with its old starting version, so it will conflict and its body will be saved as a conflict note, not lost.
sonnet.q12: The sent change is frozen. The new edit makes a new queued change with its own new change ID. If the first was accepted, the new change's starting version becomes the new version. If it conflicted, it keeps the old starting version and will conflict too. The document does not say what starting version it gets while the result is still pending.
